format.chart: 32-team double-elimination bracket with reseeding at every stage (Joe, 2026-10-23). Winners bracket stages of 16/8/4/2/1 series counting the opening round; losers bracket stages of 8/8/4/4/2/2/1/1, alternating survivor-only and drop-in rounds; grand final plus one reset series if the one-loss finalist wins the first final. 62 series total, 63 with the reset. At every stage the pool is reseeded by original tournament seed and paired highest vs lowest, second-highest vs second-lowest, so the top seed always draws the lowest-seeded survivor. See BRACKET.md.
format.home_pattern: 2-2-1-1-1, higher seed home first (Joe, 2026-10-23): Games 1-2 higher seed, 3-4 lower seed, 5 higher seed, 6 lower seed, 7 higher seed.
format.formation_gate: A stage forms only when every series feeding it is complete: Winners Round 2 and Losers Round 1 form when all 16 opening series finish; each later stage forms when its feeding stage finishes (plus the corresponding winners stage for losers drop-in stages). No pairing exists before its stage forms (Joe's reseeding rule, 2026-10-23).
format.final: Winners-bracket champion (undefeated) vs losers-bracket champion (one loss), best of 7; if the one-loss team wins, one reset series decides the championship.

stat_keying: Player stats are stored per (team, player_id). A player rostered by two teams has one line per team, never merged.

carry.rotation_note: Series complete, Boston 4-3. Starters in the box scores: Boston Martinez, Clemens, Young, Wood, Grove, Martinez, Clemens; Tampa Bay Price, Shields, Snell, McClanahan, Kazmir, Price, Shields.

narratives.text: In Game 1, Pedro Martinez threw a no-hitter, nine innings, no hits, two walks, eleven strikeouts, and Jimmie Foxx homered twice in a 6-0 win.

In Game 2, Roger Clemens struck out fourteen over 7.1 innings; Toby Hall's sixth-inning homer gave Tampa Bay its first lead of the series, and Boston answered with three runs in the bottom of the inning against a fatigued James Shields, Jonathan Papelbon closing the 3-1 win.

In Game 3, Blake Snell threw a complete-game shutout, three hits and eight strikeouts, and the only run scored in the bottom of the ninth: Carl Crawford doubled off Cy Young and Joey Wendle doubled him home off Papelbon.

In Game 4, all six Tampa Bay runs were charged to Smoky Joe Wood, on Jason Bartlett's three-run homer in the fourth and Carlos Pena's three-run homer in the seventh; Shane McClanahan won 6-3 at 8.2 innings, and Foxx homered twice in the loss.

Game 5 was the turn of the series. Tampa Bay led 5-0 into the seventh at Fenway. Nomar Garciaparra's homer got Boston started, and the ninth produced four runs: Scott Kazmir left with a three-run lead, no outs and runners on first and third, both inherited runners scored, and Ted Williams tied the game with a single off Pete Fairbanks. Papelbon, in since the eighth, held Tampa Bay through the tenth while fatigued, and Foxx led off the bottom of the tenth with the walk-off homer, 6-5.

Tampa Bay leveled it a second time in Game 6, and did it against Martinez at his best: he threw a complete game, four hits and eleven strikeouts, and lost 3-1 because every run in the game scored in the third inning. Boston's run came home on a double play; Bartlett tripled, Hall singled him in, and Wendle hit a two-run homer. David Price walked nobody in eight innings and Fairbanks saved it.

Game 7 belonged to Clemens. He went 8.2 innings, five hits, one earned run, one walk, sixteen strikeouts, and was never fatigued. Tampa Bay's only run was Evan Longoria's fourth-inning homer. Shields broke in the fifth, when two Boston runs scored on bases-loaded walks against his fatigued reads, and Boston ran the score to 8-1. Papelbon recorded the final out.

carry.rotation_note: Series complete, Detroit 4-2. Starters in the box scores: Detroit Newhouser, Verlander, Lolich, Bridges, Morris, Newhouser; Arizona Johnson, Schilling, Webb, Gallen, Kelly, Johnson.

narratives.text: In Game 1, Randy Johnson threw eight scoreless innings of four-hit ball at Tiger Stadium; Arizona's runs came on singles off Hal Newhouser in the fourth and fifth, and the closer rule lifted Johnson at 24 outs with the two-run lead, Jose Valverde finishing the 2-0 shutout.

In Game 2, Arizona won 7-5 in thirteen innings. Detroit's three-run sixth, on Hank Greenberg's two-run triple, took a 4-3 lead; Corbin Carroll tied it with a seventh-inning homer, Gabriel Moreno's tenth-inning squeeze put Arizona ahead, Charlie Gehringer answered with a leadoff homer, and Ketel Marte's two-run homer in the thirteenth won it, Byung-Hyun Kim getting George Kell with the bases loaded for the save after Valverde was ejected for hitting Bill Freehan a second time.

In Game 3, Detroit's first inning decided it: Ty Cobb singled and stole second, Gehringer tripled him home and Al Kaline singled in a second run, and Mickey Lolich allowed three hits in seven innings in a 4-1 win. Harry Heilmann, starting in left field under Joe's lineup ruling, doubled and scored in the seventh. Freehan was ejected in the first inning, before he batted, for arguing a rare-play call.

In Game 4, Tommy Bridges threw a three-hitter with thirteen strikeouts and no Arizona runner reached third; Zac Gallen pitched a complete game and lost 3-0 on two earned runs. Willie Hernandez, capped at three outs by the rest rule, had to be lifted in the ninth in a save situation, and Denny McLain recorded the save.

Game 5 was played twice, and only the second playing counts. Jack Morris was scoreless into the eighth and Merrill Kelly threw a complete-game one-hitter and lost: George Kell's two-run triple was Detroit's only hit, and the third run scored hitless in the seventh on two Arizona errors and a squeeze. Hernandez saved the 3-1 win. The first playing, an 8-5 Arizona win, was set aside by Joe's ruling and is not in this archive.

Game 6 ended the series in Arizona. Detroit scored five runs with two out in the third off Johnson, Heilmann's three-run homer the decisive swing, and a sixth run in the fourth ended Johnson's night on the six-run fatigue line. Newhouser won 10-3, and Hernandez pitched the last three innings scoreless for the save, escaping a bases-loaded, no-out jam in the seventh.

The first playing (2026-10-26, St. Louis 10, Colorado 8, seed 20261301) was set aside by Joe's ruling of 2026-10-27 after he had the game played fresh as a co-managed human audit, and the fresh playing (2026-10-27, St. Louis 7, Colorado 2, seed 20261311, Bob Gibson a complete-game win, Ubaldo Jimenez the loss, no save, no substitution and no rare play) stands as the official Game 1 recorded here, built from the adopted state file (payoff-pitch-rockies/state_series_stl_col_g1.json, a byte copy of the candidate state state_series_stl_col_g1_comanaged_candidate_seed20261311.json) by record_r1_05_g1_replacement_pp.py with the same field mapping as the original recording; the superseded playing is preserved in the series home (archive/replaced/PP_R1_05_G1_seed20261301.md and its state file) and recorded nowhere in this archive. The series is complete, St. Louis winning 4-0, and Games 2 to 4 append the same way the original recording described. Colorado plays in the host engine's 'OPP' guest slot, so the state file keys the Rockies as 'OPP'; those keys map to COL in the records. Field mapping: rolls holds the FAC flip history (card number and draw purpose), the Payoff Pitch equivalent of the dice record; final_grades is empty because Payoff Pitch has no letter grades, and pitcher fatigue end states are in fatigue_end_states, from the fix layer stored in the state; resolutions and n41 are null because those APBA counters do not exist in Payoff Pitch; batting sac is the state's single SH category, with sf and ibb null because the states do not split them; pitching lines carry hr allowed, which the states record, and hb null, which they do not record by pitcher. The adopted Game 1 contained no rare play and no substitution: no plate appearance carried an initial percentile 00, and Ozzie Smith played the whole game at shortstop. No save arose: Gibson finished the game himself, and Joe's closer branch never fired because the 9th-inning lead was 5, outside its 1-to-3 band. Availability out of the adopted Game 1 ran under the house outs convention: caps_in and caps_out carry it in the archive's encoding (player_id: max outs next game, 0 meaning unavailable, a number meaning capped at that many outs); Gibson (27 outs, a complete game) and Jimenez (17 outs) are unavailable for the next game under the fatigue layer's rows, and Boone Logan (7 relief outs) is capped at 3 outs, which caps_out carries. CASCADE NOTE: Games 2 to 4 were played on 2026-10-26 under the superseded Game 1's availability and bench-watch flags (Jason Isringhausen sat out Game 2 under the superseded game's bar and Boone Logan pitched Game 2 without this game's cap, and the bench review behind the Games 3 and 4 lineup changes was run off the superseded game's lines); by Joe's adoption ruling those games stand exactly as played and as recorded, and their records are not rewritten. Game 2 was recorded the same way by record_r1_05_g2_pp.py from state_series_stl_col_g2.json (seed 20261302, played 2026-10-26): St. Louis 8, Colorado 3, St. Louis leading 2-0. Game 2 contained one hand-resolved rare play: the Bases Empty IN-PLAY 80-84 storm entry in the bottom of the 6th (flip 83; the delay roll came up 2d6 = 8, an 80-minute delay), under which both pitchers stiffened and were replaced (Boone Logan by Matt Belisle at once, Dizzy Dean by Al Brazle for the top of the 7th) and Ken Boyer's interrupted at-bat was re-resolved on his IN-PLAY section against Belisle. Al Brazle earns the save (three-run entry state at 5-2, bases empty, and three full innings to finish; the three-inning prong independently, per the R1-04 Game 6 precedent). Jason Isringhausen was unavailable for Game 2 under Game 1's caps_out and did not appear; Al Brazle is unavailable for Game 3 under Game 2's caps_out. Game 3 was recorded the same way by record_r1_05_g3_pp.py from state_series_stl_col_g3.json (seed 20261303, played 2026-10-26): St. Louis 1, Colorado 0, at Coors Field on its real printed 2024 card, St. Louis leading 3-0. The game was hosted on the series' host engine (St. Louis's v2 engine) with the venue carried by in-process re-pointings: the park slot held the printed Coors card, the engine's halves were re-pointed so Colorado batted last as the home club in its guest slot, and init_spans was re-pointed to stamp each starter's span with the half his club actually bats in; the host engine's BALLPARK log text still says Busch Stadium, a borrowed label only. Joe's lineup rulings for Game 3 (his post-game bench review rule) are inside the record: Lou Brock started in LF in Jim Edmonds's 5th slot and Joe Medwick played CF in his own 6th slot, off his card (carded LF only, his defense priced on his carded line), for St. Louis, and Yorvit Torrealba caught in Elias Diaz's 8th slot for Colorado; Edmonds and Diaz never appeared and neither club made a substitution of any kind. The game contained no rare play. Adam Wainwright threw eight shutout innings and Aaron Cook a complete game in the loss; the only run scored in the top of the 7th (Brock walked, stole 2nd, and scored on Medwick's single). Joe's closer branch fired for the first time in the series, summoning Ryan Helsley for the bottom of the 9th (lead of one, starter at 24 outs); Helsley earns the save on every prong. Al Brazle was unavailable for Game 3 under Game 2's caps_out and did not appear; his bar covered Game 3 only. Game 3 produced no caps: its only reliever, Helsley, recorded 3 outs. Game 4 was recorded the same way by record_r1_05_g4_pp.py from state_series_stl_col_g4.json (seed 20261304, played 2026-10-26): St. Louis 10, Colorado 7, at Coors Field on its printed 2024 card, and St. Louis wins the series 4-0. Joe's Game 4 lineup ruling (his post-game bench review rule) is inside the record: Ellis Burks started at leadoff in CF in Charlie Blackmon's slot (Blackmon benched, never appeared), Yorvit Torrealba stayed at catcher (Elias Diaz never appeared), and St. Louis fielded its Game 3 nine unchanged (Brock in LF, Medwick in CF off his card); neither club made a substitution of any kind. The game contained no rare play. Game 4 was an elimination game for Colorado, so the house hard rule's starter-in-relief exception stood open for Colorado all game; it was never used (Colorado's pitchers were its starter German Marquez and the pen arms Boone Logan and Rafael Betancourt). Harry Brecheen earned the win (7.1 innings; St. Louis led wire to wire); German Marquez took the loss, lifted book-fatigued in the 5th. Ryan Helsley finished the 9th with no save: he entered with one out, the bases empty and a three-run lead, so the tying run was not on base, at bat or on deck at his entry, and his two outs are short of the one-inning prong, the same standard applied to his Game 1 finish. Errors: Joe Medwick (CF) and Harry Brecheen (P), one each, both 2-base errors on DEFENSE reads; Colorado was errorless. Game 4 produced caps for Logan and Betancourt (7 relief outs each, capped at 3), of record only: the series is complete, St. Louis advances on the winners side at 1-0 in series and Colorado drops to the losers side at 0-1, not eliminated; advance_bracket was run at completion and filled no shell (5 of 16 opening series complete).
